parsed.modern: The smell and taste seem to be the only certain tests that the nature of the thing will admit of. If a bark should have in every respect the appearance of good cinnamon, and should be proved indisputably to be the genuine bark of the cinnamon tree; yet, if it wants the cinnamon flavour, or has it but in a low degree, we reject it: and the case is the same with the oil. It is only from use and habit, or comparison with specimens of known quality, that we can judge of the goodness, either of the drugs themselves, or of their oils.
